reanchor_receipts.content:
## Findings ledger
- [D1.DOC2.F1] Capitalism is used as a label for a social system in which markets are spatially, socially, materially, and temporally unbounded, rather than merely as an economic system — dim: use_in_context — concept: capitalism — purpose: distinguish a market-centred social system from the narrower idea of a market economy — conditions: markets form the core of society and society becomes an “appendage” of markets and money — anchor: "To designate this process, the term \"capitalism\" is more appropriate than the harmless expression \"market economy.\"" — doc: religion2022 — confidence: high
- [D1.DOC2.F3] Markets are used as a self-description of society that processes dispersed knowledge and makes society communicable without providing a truthful total observation — dim: use_in_context — concept: markets — purpose: explain how society mediates and represents its own unity from participant perspectives — conditions: no observer can access society as a whole, while prices synthesize information unavailable to any one person — anchor: "Thus markets—more precisely: the neoliberal ideology of a society founded on markets—fulfill the function of what Luhmann calls a \"self-description\" of society." — doc: religion2022 — confidence: high
- [D1.DOC2.F8] Capitalism is used as a demonic, permanently restless process that converts creative possibilities into continual innovation, growth, and destruction rather than contemplation or reconciliation — dim: use_in_context — concept: capitalism — purpose: characterize the dynamic and non-finalizing structure of capitalist expansion — conditions: unbounded private property rights and competition drive ever-new visions, innovations, and exploitation of creative labor — anchor: "It is therefore not far-fetched to characterize capitalism as something \"demonic,\" as Paul Tillich (1988) did." — doc: religion2022 — confidence: high
